content_units: Brisbane Split-System Leak: Likely Situation
Because the unit still cools, has no burning smell, and starts dripping after 20–30 minutes, the   most likely issue is condensate not draining properly   rather than a major electrical failure.
Working context
- Home:   3-bedroom townhouse in Brisbane
- Symptom:   Indoor unit drips water after 20–30 minutes
- Cooling:   Still working
- Filter:   Cleaned last month
- Priority:   Least disruptive fix first
- Budget target:   Up to AUD 350
Most Likely Causes and Safe Checks
Cause   How likely   What it usually looks like   Safe check you can do   Typical repair cost (AUD)
Blocked condensate drain line or tray   Very high   Water drips from front/underside while cooling remains normal   Turn off power, inspect visible tray/drain outlet for slime/debris   150–300
Indoor unit not level or slight installation shift   High   Water overflows one side of the indoor unit   Visually check if unit looks tilted or leaking more from one side   150–350
Partial blockage from dust/sludge despite clean filter   High   Leak starts after some runtime as water builds up   Check for visible buildup around louvers and drain area   150–300
Evaporator coil icing then melting   Medium   Drip starts later; airflow may feel weaker than usual   Run on fan-only after cooling stops and see if extra water appears   200–350+
Damaged/cracked drain pan or disconnected drain hose   Medium   Persistent drip even with normal airflow   Look for leak point concentrated at one corner/edge   200–350

Low refrigerant or airflow issue beyond filter   Lower but possible   Cooling works but may be weaker, icy pipe/coil, hissing sometimes   Check if airflow is noticeably reduced or unit ices up   250–450+
Least-Disruptive Troubleshooting Order
1) Protect the area first
- Turn the unit   off   if water is reaching flooring, skirting, power points, or furniture.
- Put down towels or a shallow container under the drip.
- If there is any nearby electrical risk, switch the system off at the isolator or breaker.
2) Try a simple reset
- Leave the unit off for   30–60 minutes  .
- Then run   fan-only mode   for 15–20 minutes if available.
- After that, test cooling again.
Why this helps:
- If light icing formed on the coil, it can thaw and drain normally for a while.
3) Check airflow basics
- Make sure   all supply vents/louvers are open  .
- Confirm nothing is blocking return air intake.
- Set temperature to a normal cooling setting, around   23–25°C  , not extremely low.
Why this helps:
- Overworking the unit can contribute to icing and excess condensate.
4) Inspect the visible indoor unit surfaces
- Look for:
- heavier dripping from   one side
- visible grime/slime near the lower edge
- signs the front cover is not seated properly
- Do   not   remove internal panels beyond the normal filter access cover.
5) Check the outdoor drain discharge point if visible
- Many split systems drain through a small pipe to an exterior wall or suitable outlet.
- If you can safely identify it, see whether water is dripping there during operation.
- If the indoor unit leaks but the drain outlet is dry, a   drain blockage   becomes even more likely.
6) Avoid these DIY actions
- Do not poke wire, coat hangers, or sharp tools into the unit.
- Do not pour chemicals/bleach into the indoor unit.
- Do not open electrical covers or refrigerant components.
- Do not keep running it for hours “to see if it clears” if dripping is increasing.
When to Call a Technician

Based on your symptoms, a technician is reasonable   if the leak returns after the basic reset/checks above  . The most likely callout outcome is a   drain clean/flush or minor re-level/drain correction  , which often fits your   AUD 350   target.
Call sooner if:
- water starts leaking within minutes, not 20–30 minutes
- dripping is enough to damage paint, plaster, flooring, or cabinetry
- airflow becomes weak or the unit starts icing
- you hear gurgling, bubbling, or hissing that is new
- the unit stops cooling properly
Treat It as Urgent If Any of These Happen
- Water is near   power outlets, extension cords, or switches
- Ceiling/wall swelling, bubbling paint, or soaked plaster appears
- There is a   burning smell  , tripped breaker, or sparking
- The leak is heavy enough to create a slip risk or damage nursery/baby items
- You see repeated icing or the unit struggles badly to cool in Brisbane heat
If any of the above occurs,   stop using the unit and arrange same-day service  .
Best Next Step for Your Situation
For your case, the most sensible path is:
- Try the   off → fan-only → normal cooling retest
- Check whether the   outside drain is flowing
- If it still drips, book a technician and describe it as:
“Split-system indoor head leaking condensate after 20–30 minutes, cooling still OK, likely blocked drain or tray overflow.”
That wording helps steer the visit toward the least disruptive and most affordable fix first.
